## 3400 N Central Park Ave — Zoning & Development Assessment

**PIN:** 13-23-316-040-0000 | **Parcel resolution:** authoritative (county address records)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3 (Residential Single-Unit)** [3]. The zoning map record was last updated **August 27, 2026**; there is no recorded rezoning ordinance on this parcel (`recently_rezoned: false`). You can verify on the [City's official Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning). *Code text is current through the Council Journal of March 18, 2026 — a later amendment may not be reflected.*

---

### 2. Could You Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Probably not by right — the lot is too small under base RS-3 standards, but an exemption may apply.**

The lot is 3,616 sq ft [property data]. RS-3 requires **2,500 sq ft of lot area per dwelling unit** [1], meaning the base calculation allows only 1 unit (3,616 ÷ 2,500 = 1.4 → 1 unit). A two-flat would require **5,000 sq ft** under base standards.

**However**, [1] provides an exemption: if **60% or more of the lots fronting the same side of the street between the two nearest intersecting streets** are already lawfully improved with multi-unit buildings — or the parcel falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries — the per-unit minimum drops to **1,500 sq ft for a two-unit building only**. At 3,616 sq ft, this parcel would qualify (3,616 ÷ 1,500 = 2.4 → 2 units). You would need to document the block-face conditions to assert this exemption [1].

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

From the zoning table for RS-3 [3] (§17-2-0102):

| Standard | RS-3 Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 0.9 |
| **Max height** | 30 ft |
| **Min lot area per unit** | 2,500 sq ft (base); 1,500 sq ft for two-unit building under §17-2-0303-B.1 [1] |
| **Min lot size** | 2,500 sq ft |

Setbacks are not specified in the retrieved code text — verify with [1] (§17-2-0300) or the Chicago Zoning Ordinance directly. Lot coverage figures were not in the retrieved data. FAR of 0.9 on 3,616 sq ft implies a maximum building floor area of ~3,254 sq ft, which is a meaningful constraint alongside height limits.

*These figures come from the city's zoning table and are authoritative for this district.*

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

- **Special District** — This parcel is within a designated Special District. No specific ordinance number was retrieved; verify scope with the Department of Planning & Development.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — The parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay (see §5 below).
- **ADU Eligible Area** — This parcel is in an ADU-allowed RS area [2] (§17-7-0570), enabling coach houses and conversion units under the Additional Dwelling Unit program (see §6).
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any residential development of 10+ units requiring a zoning map amendment or planned development would trigger ARO obligations. Avondale has 6 ARO-tracked projects totaling 76 affordable units in the community area, including Hairpin Lofts (25 units, 3414 W. Diversey) and Milwaukee Ave. Apts. (32 units, 3060 N. Milwaukee).
- **No Planned Development** — Not in a Planned Development.
- **No landmark/historic designation** — Not a Chicago landmark, not in a landmark or historic district, not on the National Register.
- **No Special Service Area** — No SSA applies.
- **No lakefront protection** — Does not apply.
- **Flood zone: X** — FEMA designation "Area of Minimal Flood Hazard." Not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not federally required.
- **Brownfield sites nearby** — Two EPA-listed brownfield properties (BNSF Little Village Paseo Segments 1 & 2) are in the broader area. Environmental due diligence is advisable before any ground disturbance.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit-Related Reduction

This parcel is **transit-served** (CTA TOD overlay). Under §17-10-0102-B, the minimum off-street parking requirement can be **reduced by up to 100%** — meaning parking could potentially be eliminated entirely for qualifying uses. Off-street parking in RS districts must generally be located on the same lot as the dwelling units served [4] (§17-10-0601-B), and is prohibited within 20 feet of the front property line or in side setbacks except via permitted driveway [4] (§17-10-0601-A).

The nearest CTA rail is **Addison (Blue Line)**, approximately 0.25 miles away. The nearest Metra is **Irving Park (Union Pacific Northwest)**, approximately 0.9 miles away.

> **Note:** RS-3 receives **no density, FAR, or height bonus** from transit proximity — those bonuses apply only in dash-3 districts (B/C and D districts). Only parking relief applies here.

---

### 6. Coach House / ADU — Can You Add One?

**Yes, potentially — this parcel is in an ADU Eligible Area** [2] (§17-7-0570), which permits coach houses in designated RS zones. Key conditions and limits under §17-9-0200 [5]:

- A coach house on an RS lot **must comply with §17-7-0570** [5] (§17-9-0201-F.1) — the ADU pre-certification process enforced by the Department of Housing [2].
- Coach houses **may not exceed 22 feet in building height** [5] (§17-9-0201-F.5); rooftop features also capped at 22 ft above grade [5].
- At least **3 feet of unobstructed open space** must be provided between the coach house and at least one side property line for the full length of the building wall, except where a side property line abuts an alley or street [5] (§17-9-0201-F.7).
- Coach houses **may be established without accessory parking** to serve the coach house unit itself [5] (§17-9-0201-F.4); parking required for the principal building may be reduced or waived via administrative adjustment [5] (§17-9-0201-F.3).
- The parcel already has 5 units per county records — the Department of Housing (ADU pre-certification) and the Department of Buildings (permit) would need to assess whether an additional unit is feasible given existing density and structure.

**Important caveat:** The lot is 3,616 sq ft on a 2-story, 5-unit masonry building built in 1927. The existing unit count (5 units) already significantly exceeds what RS-3 would allow for new construction on this lot size. This suggests the current use may be a legal nonconforming structure. Adding an ADU/coach house on a nonconforming lot may face additional scrutiny — confirm with the Department of Housing and Department of Buildings before proceeding.
